meta.plan: 2021 Citizens Redistricting Commission maps (Assembly and Senate), in effect from the 2022 election
meta.plan_note: Fiscal years before 2022-23 were collected while the 2011 maps were in force; the filter always uses the current 2021 maps. Senate terms are staggered, and every Senate seat has been elected on the 2021 map since the 2024 election.
meta.source: District boundaries: Census TIGER/Line 2026 state legislative districts, which match the Commission's final maps. Agency boundaries: TIGER/Line 2026 incorporated places, counties and school districts; CAL FIRE, CSDA, DWR and county layers for special districts (see legislative/sources.csv). Population: 2020 census blocks (PL 94-171) with the Commission's block equivalency files (Statewide Database copies).
meta.method: A city, county or school district counts in a district when their TIGER polygons overlap by at least 1 square meter in California Albers (EPSG:3310); polygons that only share an edge do not count. A special district counts in a district when a 2020 census block whose interior point lies inside its polygon belongs to that district, or when its polygon, shrunk by 50 meters because those layers do not share TIGER's edges, still overlaps the district by 10,000 square meters or by 0.5% of its area, whichever is smaller. share is the fraction of the agency's 2020 residents in the districts listed, from block interior points; area_share is the fraction of its area. A district holding under 1% of the agency's residents (or none) is an edge contact.
meta.caveat: An agency counts in an Assembly or Senate district when at least 1% of its 2020 residents live there (an agency with no residents counts in every district its territory reaches); districts it touches with fewer residents are shown as edge contacts but left out of filters and totals, and many agencies still count in more than one district, so district totals overlap.
